item.title: Tsiamalili calls for rugby reform
item.description: Former Papua New Guinea rugby representative Peter Tsiamalili Jnr has called for stronger administration and accountability in rugby union. The Works and Highways Minister and Bougainville Regional MP made the comments while attending the Rosso Trans Highway Sevens in Lae.
item.content:encoded:
Former Papua New Guinea rugby representative Peter Tsiamalili Jnr has called for stronger administration and accountability in rugby union.

The Works and Highways Minister and Bougainville Regional MP made the comments while attending the Rosso Trans Highway Sevens in Lae.

Tsiamalili alleges that poor administration and personal interests have affected the code over the past decade.

“The code has suffered because of bad administration and that has caused this sport to go to the lowest it has been,” Tsiamalili Jnr said.

“There is so much opportunity but because of self greed and self interest over rugby union, it has caused rugby union to drop.”

He also questioned the accountability of K10 million that was provided to PNG Rugby through Kumul Petroleum Holdings Limited.

“PNG Rugby has to respond to the government on the K10 million that was provided to them by KPHL, a few years back” he added.

“That has been one of the biggest hurdle that they haven’t been able to come clear on.”

Tsiamalili Jar said rugby also needs a clearer pathway for young players to progress from local competitions to national representation.

“Now we are just playing tournaments but there is no clear pathway for players for representation because we are suspended by Oceania Rugby.”

He warned that without such opportunities, talented players have been moving to other sporting codes.

“The other code (rugby league) now promises them that there is a pathway to get to the PNG Chiefs,” he said

The former national representative said rugby still has significant potential and urged administrators to put the code in order.

item.title: Karkar boat missing at sea with 11 people onboard
item.description: Search and rescue teams are still out at sea in Madang frantically trying to locate a missing dinghy with eleven people onboard. The incident occurred just a day after students from the PNG Maritime College carried out a public awareness at the Bates Oval in Madang Town on the safety of small crafts and the need for people to start adhering with safety regulations stipulated in the Small Craft Act
item.content:encoded:
Search and rescue teams are still out at sea in Madang frantically trying to locate a missing dinghy with eleven people onboard.

The incident occurred just a day after students from the PNG Maritime College carried out a public awareness at the Bates Oval in Madang Town on the safety of small crafts and the need for people to start adhering with safety regulations stipulated in the Small Craft Act.

The 23- footer boat departed Kubugam boat stop on the north coast for Karkar Island at 6 pm yesterday, but never reached its destination.

Passengers on the boat raised an alarm through a video footage, which they captured on a mobile phone around 7 pm when the boat's engine, a 60hp, encountered problems and it started taking in water from the high seas.

Relatives on the island upon receiving the message immediately organised and dispatched search parties last night.

Search and rescue efforts are continuing today.

Benson Taur, a community leader from Dumad Village, where the missing boat is from, relayed the distress message through NBC Madang last night on the station's community message segment, calling on coastal villagers along the north coast, Manam Island and Bogia to be on the lookout for the missing boat and its passengers.

Amongst the passengers were two females.

According to Mr Taur, the boat was also carrying cement bags and other building materials for the new South Karkar LLG chamber and may have been overloaded.

Meanwhile, Captain Carl Kamang of the National Maritime Safety Authority [NMSA] office in Madang said on Friday, during an awareness session, that ignorance of basic safety regulations is the number one cause of mishaps at sea.

"NMSA and other relevant authorities continue to conduct awareness on safety at sea, even before the Small Craft Act became a law in 2011. But ignorance by boat owners, operators, and even passengers is a big issue. They don't listen to the advice we give. They are simply ignorant, and that is why they will continue to face problems at sea.

According to statistics released by the Provincial Disaster Director for Madang, Rudolph Mongalee; on Friday, during the awareness, Karkar and Bagabag islands account for 50 per cent of the boating incidences that occur in Madang waters.

Mr Mongalee stated that the statistics reflect the level of ignorance by seafarers from the two islands.

He also reiterated the need for people to comply with the weather reports that are provided daily by the National Weather Service.

Madang Province is continuing to experience rough and high seas.

The Office of the Member for Sumkar is fully aware of the situation and is actively involved in the ongoing search and rescue efforts.

The MV Suguman, Sumkar DDA's vessel; has been deployed to assist with the search operation, while a drone is also being used to conduct aerial surveillance and cover areas that may be difficult to access from the sea.

The MP's office remains in close contact with the relevant authorities and communities as the operation continues.

Every available resource is being utilised to assist in locating the missing boat and people.

The office will provide further updates as verified information becomes available.

item.title: Former Magarima MP arrested over perjury allegations
item.description: Former Magarima MP Francis Potape has been arrested and charged with four counts relating to alleged perjury, fabrication of evidence and conspiracy. Potape was arrested by Criminal Investigation Division [CID] officers at Jacksons Domestic Terminal in Port Moresby on September 24.
item.content:encoded:
Former Magarima MP Francis Potape has been arrested and charged with four counts relating to alleged perjury, fabrication of evidence and conspiracy.

Potape was arrested by Criminal Investigation Division [CID] officers at Jacksons Domestic Terminal in Port Moresby on September 24.

The 54-year-old, from Huluma village in the Komo-Magarima District of Hela Province, was arrested at about 6:17pm and taken to the CID Office at Police Headquarters in Konedobu.

Police said his rights were administered under Section 42(2) of the Constitution before he was formally charged.

Director CID, Detective Superintendent Joel Simatab, said in his major incident brief that police investigations identified and confirmed that Election Petition No. 3 of 2017 was built on lies and conspiracies.

Police allege that 57 affidavits tendered as evidence in court, including Potape's affidavit, Electoral Commission Forms 66A and 66B, and photographs, were fabricated.

Police further allege that Potape, together with Paul J. Othas and lawyer Ralf Jerome, fabricated affidavits and counselled witnesses to sign them as deponents.

Police also allege that some witnesses were bribed and made to sign the affidavits while under the influence of alcohol at Martha's Guest House in Mt Hagen. Police said the witnesses later claimed their affidavits did not reflect what happened during the counting process.

Potape was detained at Boroko Police Station before being released on K10,000 bail. He is expected to appear in court next week.

item.title: Government offices locked out over outstanding rent
item.description: Several government departments have been locked out of their offices over millions of kina in outstanding rental payments. Among them is the National Disaster Centre, which has been locked out of Kitpeng Haus since last week, NBC National News has confirmed.
item.content:encoded:
Several government departments have been locked out of their offices over millions of kina in outstanding rental payments.

Among them is the National Disaster Centre, which has been locked out of Kitpeng Haus since last week, NBC National News has confirmed.

The timing of the lockout has raised concerns, particularly as the country continues to face the impacts of El Niño, with the peak now extended to the end of the year.

NBC National News contacted the Minister for National Disaster and Emergency Management, Dr Billy Joseph, for clarification on the amount owed to a named property owner. The Minister said he would provide feedback.

The Department of Information and Communication Technology [DICT] also faced a similar situation after being locked out of its offices for two days.

DICT Secretary Steven Matainaho told NBC National News that the department is now operating after the government paid K1.4 million towards outstanding rental arrears of K3.8 million.

Meanwhile, Nurses Association President Fredrick Kebai has called on the government to ensure outstanding rental payments for government agencies are settled on time to avoid disruptions to essential services.

Several attempts have been made to obtain a response from the government on the outstanding rental payments.

item.title: Two senior electoral officers suspended
item.description: Two senior officers of the Papua New Guinea Electoral Commission have been suspended for serious allegations in office. They are former acting Electoral Commissioner Margaret Vagi and deputy Kila Vaname.
item.content:encoded:
Two senior officers of the Papua New Guinea Electoral Commission have been suspended for serious allegations in office.

They are former acting Electoral Commissioner Margaret Vagi and deputy Kila Vaname.

With six months remaining before the issue of Writs in April, the body responsible for conducting elections is under public scrutiny, following the internal suspension of the two Deputy Commissioners.

Concerns have been raised that their suspension will affect election planning and preparations, adding it may be politically motivated.

NBC National News visited the PNGEC headquarters, and confirmed the suspension, however officers were reluctant to release any further information.

A statement was later released by the Electoral Commissioner Dr Nicole Haley, who is currently overseas, confirming that administrative actions have been taken, which includes the suspension of several senior officers in the interest of sound public financial management.

She said the suspension is an outcome of ongoing audit preparation activities, including the initial review of the PNGEC's financial and administrative records for the period 2020 - 2026.

This also raises questions about the initial K50 million released by the Finance Department for election preparation.

Dr Haley says the Commission found serious administrative and financial irregularities demanding immediate intervention to safeguard public funds, state assets and the integrity of the institution.

Meantime, Chairman of the Special Parliamentary Committee on Elections, Allan Bird says the suspension of the two senior heads of the Commission is deeply concerning, with elections few months away.

He said a parliamentary inquiry will be conducted in the next two weeks into the matter and others.

item.title: Maritime industry in PNG urged to turn policy into practice
item.description: Papua New Guinea’s maritime industry has been urged to turn policies and international standards into practical action to improve safety, strengthen skills and support the country’s economic development. The call was made by Chief Marine Pilot Captain Max Stossell during World Maritime Day celebrations hosted by Niugini Pilots Limited on Thursday this week.
item.content:encoded:
Papua New Guinea’s maritime industry has been urged to turn policies and international standards into practical action to improve safety, strengthen skills and support the country’s economic development.

The call was made by Chief Marine Pilot Captain Max Stossell during World Maritime Day celebrations hosted by Niugini Pilots Limited on Thursday this week.

The event brought together representatives from maritime regulators, ports, shipping operators, service providers and other key players in the industry.

World Maritime Day is observed annually to recognise the important contribution of the maritime industry to international trade, economic development and sustainable development.

The maritime sector is particularly important to Papua New Guinea because the country relies heavily on shipping to move goods, connect communities and maintain links with international markets.

Globally, more than 80 per cent of international trade by volume is carried by sea. It makes shipping industry a major part of the global economy.

This year’s World Maritime Day theme, set by the International Maritime Organization [IMO], is “From Policy to Practice: Powering Maritime Excellence.”

The theme focuses on ensuring that international maritime policies, regulations and standards are translated into practical action through proper implementation, training, enforcement and safety measures.

Captain Stossell said the theme was relevant to the industry because having laws and standards alone was not enough.

"While legislation and standards provide the foundation for a safe and effective maritime sector, policies only fulfill their purpose when implemented consistently, competently, and transparently.” he said.

He said maritime excellence required competent professionals, continuous career development, strong legislation, accountable enforcement and effective regulatory institutions.

He also highlighted the need for proper training and modern equipment, supported by strong safety management systems.

Captain Stossell said the maritime industry was becoming more complex as ports became busier and vessels became larger and more technologically advanced.

"Our maritime sector serves as a vital lifeline, connecting us both domestically and globally.

"It drives international trade, supplies our local communities, and contributes significantly to our economic development,” he said.

The Chief Mariner said Papua New Guinea must continue investing in its maritime professionals by expanding training and strengthening competency assessments.

He also called for stronger institutional capacity so regulatory bodies like the National Maritime Safety Authority [NMSA] can effectively carry out their responsibilities and meet international maritime standards.

For Captain Stossell, safety must become part of the daily culture of the industry rather than simply a requirement under the law.

"We must ensure that turning policy into practice is not just a slogan, but an ongoing mission that yields safer ships, cleaner oceans, stronger institutions, and a resilient maritime industry for Papua New Guinea and the world.” he said.

Meanwhile, the World Maritime Day celebration also recognised the men and women working across Papua New Guinea’s maritime sector.

From pilots and seafarers to regulators, port workers, shipping companies and service providers, each plays a role in keeping the country’s maritime lifeline operating.

The event provided an opportunity for the industry to reflect on its contribution while renewing its commitment to safety, professional development, innovation and continuous improvement.

For Papua New Guinea, the message from the celebration is clear and that is strong maritime policies must be matched by practical action to keep the country’s waters, ports, vessels and people safe.

item.title: 2026 Rosso Trans Highway 7s kicks off in Lae
item.description: The 2026 Rosso Trans Highway 7s has officially kicked off at Scrum Oval in Lae, with the Lae City Pipes and Drums opening the tournament program. Works Minister Peter Tsiamalili Jr officially opened the tournament, with Lae MP and Deputy Prime Minister John Rosso and Huon District MP Jason Peter also in attendance.
item.content:encoded:
The 2026 Rosso Trans Highway 7s has officially kicked off at Scrum Oval in Lae, with the Lae City Pipes and Drums opening the tournament program.

Works Minister Peter Tsiamalili Jr officially opened the tournament, with Lae MP and Deputy Prime Minister John Rosso and Huon District MP Jason Peter also in attendance.

The first match saw PC Ravens take on Gonix Pirates as competition got underway in the three-day tournament, which runs from September 25 to 27.

The tournament features Open Men’s, Under-20 and Women’s divisions, with 24 teams drawn into six pools in the Open Men’s competition.

Pool A: PC Ravens, Gonix Pirates, Galio Tati Bards, Tararan Sagasek Pool B: Barbarians, Irok Pirates, JKT Lim Vikings, Gerehu Native Pool C: Kinabot Piggies, Kimbe Rebels, Chemcare Defence, Lae Harlequins Pool D: Goroka Kingsmen, Black Orchid, Tent City Light, DYY Spartans Pool E: Goroka Harlequins, Hangan Pirates, New Town Chiefs, Unitech Reds Pool F: Rabaul Stallions, Patuki Warriors, Malac Wanderers, Kabrats

The Under-20 competition has four pools, while five teams are competing in the Women’s division.

The tournament also features live entertainment, with Kronos performing tonight, Friday, September 25, and Leonard Kania scheduled to perform on Sunday, September 27.

Competition continues throughout the weekend at Scrum Oval, with rugby supporters encouraged to turn out and support the teams.

item.title: Madang police urge illegal gun owners to surrender them
item.description: Madang Provincial Police Commander Superintendent Robert Baim is urging people in possession of illegal firearms to surrender them to police during the extended national gun amnesty. The National Executive Council has extended the gun amnesty for another four months, with the new deadline set for December 25, 2026.
item.content:encoded:
Madang Provincial Police Commander Superintendent Robert Baim is urging people in possession of illegal firearms to surrender them to police during the extended national gun amnesty.

The National Executive Council has extended the gun amnesty for another four months, with the new deadline set for December 25, 2026.

Superintendent Baim said the extension provides an opportunity for people holding illegal weapons to voluntarily surrender them and help remove firearms from circulation.

“Many firearms are in the wrong hands and contribute directly to criminal activities and serious harm to innocent people. Police are, therefore, urging all persons who are in possession of illegal guns, whether knowingly or otherwise, to do the right thing and surrender them during the amnesty period,” he said.

He said people who surrender illegal firearms during the amnesty can do so without facing arrest, provided they follow the required police processes and procedures.

Police will also work with relevant authorities and community stakeholders to make the surrender process accessible across the province, including in remote and rural areas.

However, Superintendent Baim warned that strict enforcement action would follow once the amnesty period ends.

“Police will not tolerate anyone still holding onto illegal guns after the end of the amnesty period. Those found in possession of illegal firearms after the amnesty will face severe penalties under the newly amended Firearms Act,” he said.

He said illegal firearms pose a serious threat to communities and that police remain committed to protecting lives and maintaining public safety.

People wishing to surrender firearms are advised to contact the appropriate police authorities to arrange a safe handover.

item.title: One more bridge goes down in Madang
item.description: One more bridge along the Madang/ Bogia Highway gave way and collapsed this morning, disrupting the flow of traffic between Madang and Bogia.

item.title: Pacific Governments urged to take journalists on overseas trips
item.description: Prime Ministers Department and other government agencies in the Pacific have been urged to involve mainstream media journalists in international engagements involving senior political leaders.
